content.text: A highly contagious skin infect ← mite
burrow into skin to lay eggs, feed, & defecate
(scybala are fecal particles that precipitate a hypersensitivity rxn in skin) - pruritic response to mite itself · mite feces · mite eggs

spread via prolonged skin-to-skin contact - intense pruritus · burrows · excoriations commonly seen in other family members - esp family members or sexual partners - casual contact less likely - fomites (clothes · bed linens) poss but less common

any age & socioeconomic status - female mite burrows into epidermis → eggs → larvae → adult mites - USU ⍉transmitted from animals - fomites less common in classic scabies (↓parasite burden) - crusted scabies → ↑parasite burden → more likely fomite spread
Infected pts may remain w.o sxs for up to 4-6wks - sxs begin w.in 3-6wks of primary infestation · w.in 3d of 2ndry infestation
b/n fingers & toes - USU spares neck & face - S-shaped burrows typically in web spaces of fingers

•MC sites: extremities incl palms · soles · wrists · axillae · waist · genitalia · buttocks - back & scalp USU spared except young children - also extensor elbows or knees · periareolar · periumbilical · male genitalia · lower buttocks & adjacent thighs · lateral or posterior ft
•burrows: 2-15mm thin serpiginous lines - can mimic excoriations - may ⍉be visible if excoriations or 2ndry infect
red itchy pruritic papules or nodules on scrotum · glans · penile shaft or body folds
•crusted scabies: scaly · warty · malodorous lesions - pruritus less characteristic - IS · older adults · Down syndrome
•comp: impetigo · ecthyma · paronychia · furunculosis - untx → sepsis in IS - untx crusted scabies → can spread to entire skin
•thick · crusted · fissured plaques in older or IS pt → crusted scabies
